questions.q: What is the defining trait of best-of-breed multi-cloud, as this lesson describes it?
options: Every workload must run on at least two providers simultaneously
Each individual workload still runs on exactly one cloud; the multi-cloud-ness lives at the portfolio level across different workloads
The company must spend an equal dollar amount with each provider
Only machine-learning workloads are allowed to use a second provider
questions.explain: In best-of-breed multi-cloud, no single workload is duplicated — each one runs on whichever provider suits it best, and the organization's overall portfolio simply spans more than one cloud.

questions.q: What does redundancy-driven multi-cloud actually mean?
options: Running the same workload, in parallel or hot standby, on two different providers so a provider-level outage can't take it down
Buying redundant internet connections from the same cloud provider
Running every workload on three or more clouds instead of two
Switching providers every year to negotiate a better price
questions.explain: Redundancy-driven multi-cloud duplicates an entire workload across two providers specifically for resilience against a provider-wide failure, unlike best-of-breed, which keeps each workload on one cloud.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say redundancy-driven multi-cloud is substantially more expensive than best-of-breed multi-cloud?
options: Because redundant workloads are always billed at a premium rate by cloud providers
Because redundancy-driven multi-cloud is illegal without a special license
Because best-of-breed multi-cloud requires no networking between providers at all
Because every change must be designed, built, and validated twice to keep two independent implementations behaviorally equivalent
questions.explain: With redundancy-driven multi-cloud, the same workload is built and maintained as two separate implementations that must stay in sync, roughly doubling engineering, testing, and operational cost — not just infrastructure spend.

questions.q: What distinguishes active-active from active-passive redundancy-driven multi-cloud?
options: Active-active uses containers, while active-passive never does
Active-active is only used for databases, never for application servers
In active-active, both copies serve real traffic simultaneously; in active-passive, one copy sits ready to take over on failover
Active-passive runs on three clouds while active-active runs on two
questions.explain: Active-active and active-passive are the two forms redundancy-driven multi-cloud can take, differing in whether both provider copies handle live traffic at once or one stands by for failover.

questions.q: What question does the lesson say every multi-cloud proposal should answer before it's approved?
options: Whether the proposal uses the word 'cloud-native' enough times
Whether it's a single workload moving to a better-suited provider (best-of-breed) or the same workload being built twice to survive an outage (redundancy-driven)
Whether the CFO has personally approved the specific dollar figure
Whether the proposal includes a logo for each provider involved
questions.explain: Because best-of-breed and redundancy-driven multi-cloud have very different cost and complexity profiles, a vague proposal should be sent back until it specifies which shape of multi-cloud it actually is.
